properties.name: BL-159: the two records of the build-gate contract are now cross-checked by the build. AGENTS.md's "A change is done when all of these are clean" block and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` were two hand-kept records of one contract, and following the documented one exactly still produced a red build (PR #27). `skill_lint.py` now fails if a `cargo`/`python3` gate in ci.yml appears in NEITHER the block nor the blockquote that names deliberate omissions, if a listed command is spelled differently from the way CI runs it, or if either list names a gate CI has stopped running. FOUR CHECKS RATHER THAN THE ROW'S ONE, and the extra one is the load-bearing one: the row proposed COVERAGE only, but the defect that filed BL-159 was a FLAGS difference on a gate that WAS listed (`-p reflow2-core` clippy lacking `-D warnings`), which coverage alone cannot see — so identity and fidelity are checked separately. THE SPLIT THAT KEEPS IT HONEST is BL-160's threshold lesson again: the lint OBSERVES (is this ci.yml line a gate at all — mechanical, in code), the document JUDGES (does it belong in the everyday local subset — in AGENTS.md, where a human reads it). FOUND ON DAY ONE, which is the payoff: `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` and `test_check_doc_versions` were in ci.yml and in neither list. The second is the trap the design anticipated — `check_doc_versions` is a substring of `test_check_doc_versions`, so a substring match would have reported the second as already covered; matching is exact on the script stem. THE CHECK CAUGHT A DEFECT IN ITSELF on its own commit: scanning the whole blockquote read the backticked words `cargo` and `python3` out of the new paragraph describing the lint and reported them as gates CI had stopped running. REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: reverting the first-paragraph scoping ALONE leaves every check green, because the runner-word exclusion covers today's prose — the two are not redundant in general, and the scoping is pinned on synthetic text where the redundancy cannot hide it.
